note: Webform Encrypt encrypts individual webform element values at rest using an Encrypt encryption profile. It has NO settings form and NO configure route (configure=null). Its only persistent config is a per-element third-party setting on the webform: webform.webform.<id> -> third_party_settings.webform_encrypt.element.<key> = {encrypt: true, encrypt_profile: <profile_id>}. At runtime hook_entity_type_alter swaps the webform_submission storage class to WebformEncryptSubmissionStorage (encrypts in doPreSave, decrypts in doPostSave/loadData; serialized as {data, encrypt_profile}) and the access handler to WebformEncryptSubmissionAccessControlHandler. The single permission 'view encrypted values' gates decrypting values (placeholder '[Value Encrypted]' otherwise) and editing submissions containing encrypted elements. Medium/hard cases are grounded in that real third-party-settings config, verified against the live webform config entity. Setup/reset scripts create an Encrypt profile we_test_profile (+ key we_test_key) and webforms prefixed we_encrypt_.

evals.prompt: In Drupal, I enabled the webform_encrypt module but there is no settings page for it. How do I turn on encryption for one field of a webform, and where exactly is that choice stored in configuration?
evals.expected_output: There is no configure route. On the element's Advanced tab tick 'Encrypt this field's value' and choose an encryption profile. It is stored as a per-element third-party setting on the webform: webform.webform.<id> -> third_party_settings.webform_encrypt.element.<element_key> = {encrypt: true, encrypt_profile: <id>}.

evals.prompt: With the Drupal webform_encrypt module, which permission controls whether a user sees the real decrypted submission values, and what do users without it see?
evals.expected_output: The 'view encrypted values' permission. Users lacking it see the placeholder text '[Value Encrypted]' instead of decrypted data, and are also forbidden from editing (updating) submissions that contain encrypted elements.

evals.prompt: How does the Drupal webform_encrypt module actually encrypt submission data when a webform is saved? Which entity handler does it replace and where does the encryption happen?
evals.expected_output: hook_entity_type_alter swaps the webform_submission storage class to WebformEncryptSubmissionStorage, which encrypts flagged element values in doPreSave() (using core's 'encryption' service and the element's encryption profile) and decrypts them again in doPostSave()/loadData(). It also swaps the access control handler to WebformEncryptSubmissionAccessControlHandler.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a webform with machine name 'we_encrypt_known' that has one element configured to be encrypted by webform_encrypt. Inspect the live webform configuration and give the machine name (key) of the encrypted element.
evals.expected_output: The element is 'ssn'. In webform.webform.we_encrypt_known the third_party_settings.webform_encrypt.element.ssn entry has encrypt: true (profile we_test_profile).

evals.prompt: The webform 'we_encrypt_profile' on this site encrypts its 'card' element with webform_encrypt. Inspect the live configuration and state which encryption profile is used to encrypt that element.
evals.expected_output: The encryption profile is we_test_profile: webform.webform.we_encrypt_profile -> third_party_settings.webform_encrypt.element.card.encrypt_profile = we_test_profile.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the webform 'we_encrypt_task' has elements 'name' and 'ssn' and an encryption profile 'we_test_profile' already exists. Using the webform_encrypt module, configure the webform so that the 'ssn' element's submitted value is encrypted. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set third_party_settings.webform_encrypt.element.ssn = {encrypt: true, encrypt_profile: we_test_profile} on webform.webform.we_encrypt_task (via $webform->setThirdPartySetting('webform_encrypt','element', [...])->save(), or by ticking 'Encrypt this field's value' on the ssn element's Advanced tab).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the webform 'we_encrypt_task2' has a 'notes' textarea element, and an encryption profile named 'we_test_profile' exists. Use webform_encrypt to encrypt the 'notes' element specifically with the 'we_test_profile' encryption profile, and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: On webform.webform.we_encrypt_task2 set third_party_settings.webform_encrypt.element.notes = {encrypt: true, encrypt_profile: we_test_profile} and save.
